changes: Creates docs/requirements/decisions/red-evidence-subsystem-spec.md (1607 lines): the complete decision contract for the trusted RED-evidence subsystem (program Workstream 2). Sections: §0 scope/canon/threat-model with the assurance-tier clause; §1 assertion envelope (literal-line + registered class matchers, quantified floors, adapter-owned nonce linkage, target-binding registry, GREEN predicate + GREEN_v2 mapping table, worked valid/invalid examples, hard spec-level floors); §2 disposable-workspace runner (CLEAN/PRE/POST four-tuples, prep constraints, timeout discipline, streamFrames capture); §3 per-target supersedes chains + operationKey idempotency with pre-run dedupe; §4 owner-gated quarantine/recover + corrected retention; §5 read-only gate-consumption query (total algorithm, tagged errors, FRESH algorithm bound to isMaterialExcludedPath, W2/W3 MUST-NOT boundary); §6 legacy posture via adoption-time migration manifest. No code changed.
usage: W2 implementation stories cite the spec section-by-section as acceptance contracts (e.g. 'implement §3.4 operationKey derivation'); W3 wires gates to the §5 query. Read: docs/requirements/decisions/red-evidence-subsystem-spec.md
expectedOutcome: A PLAN-reviewed decision spec covering the program plan's five contract areas plus the gate-consumption query contract and the legacy-record posture, precise enough that implementation stories need zero design decisions at the stated assurance tier, and hardened by genuine cross-host audit.
actualTranscript: Six-round dual-host audit loop (codex + agy): 75 findings dispositioned (fixed / tier-scoped / superseded by the literal-only matcher decision); terminal verdicts agy APPROVE (unconditional) + codex APPROVE-WITH-CHANGES with all four conditions folded. Formal REVIEW: round 1 codex host-B PASS + quality/concept/test-coverage PASS + docs F-001 (a factual misbinding in §5.3, fixed and verified by its filer in round 2); round 2 all four lanes PASS. 21/21 verificationIntent lanes independently verified TRUE of the document; ~20 src file:line anchors verified; lattice validate 46/46 green.
outcomeDiff: No difference — the delivered spec covers every mandated area with the two architecture decisions (literal-only matchers; assurance-tier scoping) recorded as settled, auditor-accepted choices.
limitations: The spec targets the practical assurance tier (§0.6): accidental fabrication, workflow drift, and casual gaming; the fully hostile local agent with filesystem/toolchain control is the Tier-C signed-receipt program's adversary. A vetted pattern language beyond literal-line matchers, executable digest-binding as mandatory, and unification of isMaterialExcludedPath with W1's resolveMaterialCodePolicy are each declared separate future reviewed changes. Implementation and gate wiring belong to the W2 implementation stories and W3 respectively.
pitfalls: Dual-host spec audits do NOT converge by patching: rounds 1-5 (31/17/11/13/19 findings) each bred fresh findings from the new text. Convergence came from REMOVING unbounded surfaces (rev 6: anchored-regex deleted in favor of literal-only matchers, killing the whole regex-gaming class) plus honest tier-scoping (assurance-tier clause per the S1 pragmatic-close precedent) — after which both hosts approved in one round. Other traps: the spec author wrote to the MAIN checkout instead of the story worktree (canonical copy relocated); a spec's own factual claims about existing code need the same src-anchor verification as code reviews (docs lane caught a §5.3 misbinding all six audit rounds missed); keep summary vocabulary clear of the equivalence-gate shrinkage regex.
